clue.text: More potent, cheaper drugs distributed

indicators.note: letters distributed are spread about and set out in a fresh order

explanation.surface: Cheaper narcotics on the street are said to be stronger than ever.
explanation.walkthrough: 'distributed' looks like part of the drug-dealing picture but signals the rearrangement of CHEAPER DRUGS.
explanation.definitionFit: Something boosted beyond its normal power, as an engine with a forced air intake, is more potent.

clue.text: Having escaped fire, Polish Greek character turns up with nightclothes

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up means the letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: to rub is to polish
nu is a letter of the Greek alphabet
night clothes: the outer letters of night, N and T, clothe it

explanation.surface: Someone who escaped a blaze, buffing a Greek letter while in pyjamas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nightclothes' must be split: the word night is clothed by its outside letters, NT.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that escaped a fire was not charred or scorched, untouched by flames.

clue.text: Canines already see support rising. What about that?

indicators.note: the exclamation goes about, outside, the other pieces

parts.note: eh is a questioning exclamation, like 'what?'
yet can mean already, as in 'is it time yet?'

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means the letters read upwards

parts.note: a tee is the peg supporting a golf ball

explanation.surface: Dogs already see their support climbing, a remarkable sight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'see' and 'that' are link words. 'Canines' looks like dogs but means the pointed teeth.
explanation.definitionFit: The canine teeth of the upper jaw are traditionally called by this name.

clue.text: Clever charges undermine the expenditure caps

indicators.note: the caps are the tops, the first letters, of each word

explanation.surface: Smart fees eat away at spending limits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'caps' looks like limits on spending but signals first letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Cute in the sense of shrewd or cunning means clever.

clue.text: Charge against Luxembourg's chargés d'affaires?

parts.note: A is an abbreviation of against
L is the international vehicle code for Luxembourg
a legation is a diplomatic mission headed by an envoy or chargé d'affaires

explanation.surface: A query about accusations against Luxembourg's diplomats.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that chargés d'affaires, as a body, make a legation.
explanation.definitionFit: An allegation is a claim of wrongdoing laid against someone, an accusation.

clue.text: Part of roof beginning to buckle in storm

indicators.note: the letter sits inside the storm

parts.note: a gale is a storm wind

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Part of a roof starting to give way in high winds.
explanation.definitionFit: A gable is the triangular upper wall section beneath a pitched roof's ends.

clue.text: Party about to welcome master in charge of rodents

parts.note: a do is a party

indicators.note: the word for about welcomes the others, taking them inside

parts.note: re means about or concerning
M stands for master, as in MA

explanation.surface: A party poised to receive the master who runs things.
explanation.definitionFit: Dormice are small, mostly nocturnal rodents noted for long hibernation.

clue.text: Resist charges wrongly shown by these

definitions.text: Resist charges wrongly shown by these

indicators.note: letters set wrongly are put in a jumbled order

explanation.surface: A tip-off that a shop's tills record overcharges.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: tills could indeed display charges wrongly.
explanation.definitionFit: Shop tills display prices and charges, so they are what shows charges, wrongly or not.

clue.text: Australian tennis player's violent tram rage gets charges brought here

indicators.note: violent rage throws the letters into disorder

parts.note: criminal charges are brought before a court of law

explanation.surface: A tennis star's road rage on a tram lands her in the dock.
explanation.walkthrough: Margaret Court won a record 24 Grand Slam singles titles.
explanation.definitionFit: Margaret Court is a celebrated Australian women's tennis champion of the 1960s and 70s.

clue.text: Ban item malfunctioning in the atmosphere

indicators.note: something malfunctioning is not working properly, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A prohibited object goes wrong somewhere up in the air.
explanation.definitionFit: Ambient describes conditions of the surrounding air or environment, such as room temperature.

clue.text: State airline left first

indicators.note: first says the left letter comes before the airline's name

parts.note: Iberia is the Spanish national airline

explanation.surface: A national airline departed before the others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left' looks like the past tense of leave but supplies L.
explanation.definitionFit: Liberia is a country, a sovereign nation in West Africa, so a state.

clue.text: Charger right to wear socks

indicators.note: the right letter wears the socks, being clothed by them, so it sits within

parts.note: hose is an old word for stockings or socks

explanation.surface: Instructions on the correct way to put on one's socks.
explanation.definitionFit: A charger is a war mount, the animal a knight rode into battle.

clue.text: Consenting adult? Dyke embraces a German

parts.note: A is the film classification for adult

indicators.note: the forename hugs the German article, holding it inside

parts.note: Greg Dyke, a former director-general of the BBC
ein is German for a

explanation.surface: An adult agreeing to something while a man named Dyke hugs a German woman.
explanation.walkthrough: Dyke is not a dam but the surname of Greg Dyke, a former BBC boss, so supplying GREG.
explanation.definitionFit: Agreeing means giving assent, the same as consenting to a proposal.

clue.text: Commercial power gets people in film careful consideration, in America at least

definitions.text: careful consideration, in America at least

parts.note: an ad is a commercial
vis is Latin for force or power

indicators.note: the people go inside the film's title

parts.note: E.T. is the Spielberg film
men means people

explanation.surface: A powerful advertisement casts actors in a film.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition carries the qualifier because the word is chiefly American usage.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking something under advisement, mainly in US usage, means considering it carefully.

clue.text: Passing on charge laid out in Brussels treaty which lacks content

indicators.note: the set-forth word goes inside the union's letters

parts.note: Brussels is the seat of the European Union, EU
laid out, as of facts set forth, means stated

indicators.note: a word lacking its content keeps only its outside letters

explanation.surface: A charge imposed under a Brussels treaty that turns out to be empty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Passing on' means dying: the tax due when property passes on death.
explanation.definitionFit: This British tax was levied on a dead person's property, a charge on passing on.

clue.text: Drop charge

definitions.meaning: a teardrop, a single drop from the eye
to rush headlong, as to charge or ... down the street

explanation.surface: Drop charges.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is a drop of eye water; the other is rushing at speed, like charging.

clue.text: Directly lead one through 23

indicators.note: the pieces pass through, inside, the other word

parts.note: the answer to 23 down, informal talk
Pb is the chemical symbol for lead
a means one

explanation.surface: A short instruction to lead one straight through.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lead' looks like the verb to guide but is the metal.
explanation.definitionFit: Slap-bang means exactly or directly, as in slap-bang in the middle.

clue.text: Aperitifs? Order bottles in that case

indicators.note: these words bottle, or contain, the answer within them

explanation.surface: Someone ordering pre-dinner drinks, perhaps bottles of them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bottles' looks like a noun in a drinks order but is a verb signalling letters held within the words.
explanation.definitionFit: If so is a conditional phrase meaning given that, or in that case.

clue.text: Flyer noticed list of charges

parts.note: saw means noticed
a bill is a list of charges to pay

explanation.surface: A flyer spotted a list of fees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flyer' looks like a leaflet but is a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A sawbill is a merganser, a diving duck with a serrated beak, so a bird.

clue.text: Irrational group lacking what should always be on

parts.note: pi is the best-known irrational number
a lot is a group or batch
light on something means lacking it

explanation.surface: An unreasonable gang that is short of something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Irrational' is not a description of the group: pi is an irrational number.
explanation.definitionFit: A small flame on a gas boiler or cooker is kept burning permanently to ignite the main burner.

clue.text: The gods could be haunted

indicators.note: says the letters could be rearranged into something else

explanation.surface: Perhaps the deities have been visited by spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: Ghosted can mean visited by a spirit, as a haunted house is.

clue.text: Have kinky sex among a number of people from Clacton?

indicators.note: the pieces are placed among the letters of the number

parts.note: ten is a number
to own is to have
S and M, sadomasochism, is kinky sex

explanation.surface: Kinky goings-on among the residents of a seaside resort.
explanation.walkthrough: Clacton is an Essex seaside town, so its people are town dwellers; the question mark flags the definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Residents of a town, as opposed to country folk or students, are town dwellers.

clue.text: Be rude about Pole's informal talk

indicators.note: the rude word goes about, around, the pole

parts.note: to slag, as in slag off, is to be rude about someone
N is the north pole

explanation.surface: Insulting a Polish person's casual manner of speech.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pole' looks like a Polish person but is a magnetic pole, N.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang is very informal language, colloquial talk outside standard usage.

clue.text: Powerhouse to snap

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for power and HO for house

explanation.surface: A dynamo of a person moving to bite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Powerhouse' reads as one word but splits into power (P) and house (HO).
explanation.definitionFit: A snap is a casual photograph, a snapshot.

clue.text: Starts to see pixies under rock outcrop

indicators.note: the starts of the words are their first letters

explanation.surface: Beginning to spot elves beneath a stone.
explanation.definitionFit: A spur is a projecting ridge of rock or land, an outcrop on a hillside.

clue.text: English town engineers Apple scandal?

parts.note: RE stands for the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps
Apple prefixes its products with i, and -gate is the suffix tagging a scandal

explanation.surface: Technicians manufacturing a scandal over a tech company.
explanation.walkthrough: Reigate is a town in Surrey, south of London.
explanation.definitionFit: Reigate is a market town in Surrey, south-east England.

clue.text: Charger needing drink in Puerto Rico

indicators.note: the drink goes inside the abbreviation

parts.note: a latte is a milky coffee drink

explanation.surface: A horse needing water in the Caribbean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charger' looks like a horse but is an old word for a large flat dish.
explanation.definitionFit: A charger is a large serving dish, the same as a big plate for serving.

clue.text: Illuminate a bridge ruined by chargers

parts.note: to light is to illuminate

indicators.note: a ruined structure lies in disorder, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Floodlighting a bridge damaged by cavalry.
explanation.walkthrough: BRIGADE comes from the anagram of A and BRIDGE.
explanation.definitionFit: The Charge of the Light Brigade was a famous cavalry charge, so its members were chargers.
